def: A GLP-1 receptor agonist injected for type 2 diabetes and obesity. It boosts glucose-dependent insulin release, suppresses glucagon and slows gastric emptying; risks include pancreatitis and thyroid C-cell tumors.
A DPP-4 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes that raises incretin (GLP-1) levels, increasing glucose-dependent insulin release. Cleared mainly through bile, so no renal dose adjustment is needed.

Enzyme linking glycolysis and lipid synthesis by converting dihydroxyacetone phosphate to glycerol-3-phosphate, which provides the glycerol backbone for triglycerides. Also part of the glycerol phosphate shuttle for NADH.
Hormone released by fat cells that increases insulin sensitivity and fatty acid oxidation. Levels fall in obesity and type 2 diabetes.
Tight junctions between adjacent Sertoli cells that isolate developing sperm cells from the blood. It protects haploid germ cells from immune attack because they are antigenically foreign.
Haploid male germ cell produced by meiosis II that matures into sperm (spermiogenesis) without further division. Lies close to the lumen of the seminiferous tubule.
Development of egg cells in the ovary. Oocytes arrest in prophase I from fetal life until ovulation, then in metaphase II until fertilization.
Long first stage of meiosis I in which homologous chromosomes pair and cross over, exchanging genetic material. Oocytes remain arrested in this stage (diplotene) until puberty.
Hormone of the TGF-beta family that stimulates FSH release from the pituitary. Counterbalanced by inhibin, which comes from Sertoli and granulosa cells.
Microtubule structure at the base of a cilium or flagellum that anchors and organizes it. Structurally related to a centriole.
Infrequent menstrual periods, with cycles longer than 35 days. A common feature of polycystic ovary syndrome.
Enzyme that removes sulfate groups from molecules. Lysosomal sulfatase deficiencies cause storage diseases such as Hunter syndrome and metachromatic leukodystrophy.
Sex chromosome carrying the SRY gene that drives male development. Present in males only and contains few genes beyond testis determination and spermatogenesis.
Chronic pelvic or perineal pain from irritation or entrapment of the pudendal nerve (S2-S4). Often worse when sitting.
A phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitor for erectile dysfunction that raises cGMP in penile smooth muscle. Contraindicated with nitrates because of severe hypotension.
Loss of cell differentiation and cell identity, with pleomorphism and many mitoses. A hallmark of malignancy.
Benign ovarian tumor of mucin-secreting epithelium forming large multilocular cysts. Can become very large.
Surgical removal of breast tissue to prevent cancer, considered for BRCA1 or BRCA2 carriers.
Ovarian or pancreatic cystic tumors lined by serous (watery) or mucinous (mucus-secreting) epithelium, ranging from benign to malignant.
Abdomen filled with gelatinous mucin from a mucinous tumor, usually of the appendix, that has ruptured and seeded the peritoneum.
Malignant ovarian or pancreatic cystic tumor of mucin-secreting epithelium.
Uncommon ovarian tumor of transitional-like epithelium, usually benign. Histology shows coffee-bean nuclei.
Ovarian teratoma composed mostly of thyroid tissue, which can cause hyperthyroidism.
Sex cord-stromal tumor that produces androgens and causes virilization in women. Called arrhenoblastoma.
Ovarian metastasis, usually bilateral, from a mucin-secreting signet ring cell carcinoma, classically of the stomach.
Fibrous plaque in the penile tunica albuginea causing painful curved erections.
Painless cystic collection of sperm-containing fluid in the epididymis, which transilluminates.
Formation of sperm and eggs by meiosis from germ cells.
Cystic remnant of the urachus between the bladder and umbilicus, which can become infected.
Drug that forms a protective barrier over ulcers in an acidic environment. Needs acid to work.
Electrochemical proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane that drives ATP synthase.
Low sperm concentration in semen, a cause of male infertility.
Loosely packed, transcriptionally active DNA, lightly stained.
Stretches of DNA rich in cytosine-guanine pairs, often in gene promoters. Methylation silences transcription.
Bacterial type II topoisomerase that relieves supercoiling. Target of fluoroquinolones.
Enzyme that makes short RNA primers for DNA polymerase.
Base change that doesn't alter the encoded amino acid because of codon redundancy.
Base change creating a premature stop codon, producing truncated protein.
Kinase that detects DNA double-strand breaks and activates p53. Mutated in ataxia-telangiectasia.
Parts of mRNA outside the coding sequence that regulate translation and stability.
mRNA segment after the stop codon, containing regulatory signals including the poly-A signal.
DNA sequence that increases transcription of a gene, even from a distance, by binding activator proteins.
Transcription factor activated by cAMP-dependent phosphorylation by protein kinase A.
Neural crest disorder with sensorineural deafness, white forelock and different-colored eyes.
Drug that caused limb malformations (phocomelia) in fetuses; now used for multiple myeloma and leprosy reactions.
Genus of mushrooms; Amanita phalloides contains alpha-amanitin, which inhibits RNA polymerase II and causes liver failure.
Addition of a poly-A tail to the 3' end of mRNA after transcription, protecting it and aiding export.
Chain of adenine nucleotides added to the 3' end of mRNA that stabilizes it.
Enzyme that adds the poly-A tail to the 3' end of pre-mRNA.
Degradation of mRNA that sets how long it is translated.
Cytoplasmic granules (P-bodies) where mRNA is degraded or stored.
Sequences at intron-exon boundaries recognized by the spliceosome; introns begin with GU (5' donor) and end with AG (3').
Pyrimidine nucleoside of cytosine and ribose.
RNA molecule with catalytic activity, such as the peptidyl transferase in ribosomes.
mRNA segment before the start codon containing ribosome binding signals.
Toxin that ADP-ribosylates elongation factor 2, halting protein synthesis, like diphtheria toxin.
Cell response to stress that induces chaperone proteins (heat shock proteins) to refold damaged proteins.
Amino acid whose amide nitrogen is the site of N-linked glycosylation in the ER.
Motor protein that moves cargo along microtubules toward the plus end (anterograde).
Heart positioned in the right chest; in Kartagener syndrome it occurs with situs inversus.
ATPase pumping 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ in per ATP, maintaining the resting potential. Inhibited by digoxin and ouabain.
Cardiac glycoside that inhibits the Na+/K+ ATPase.
Clear gel filling the eye between the lens and retina.
Enzyme that cuts the terminal propeptides off procollagen outside the cell; deficiency causes Ehlers-Danlos.
DNA made by joining sequences from different sources, used for cloning and producing proteins.
Bacterial enzymes cutting DNA at specific palindromic sequences, used in cloning.
Variation in DNA fragment sizes after enzyme cutting due to sequence differences, used in genetic mapping.
Technique detecting a specific DNA sequence by transferring digested DNA to a membrane and hybridizing a probe.
Short single strand of nucleotides, used as a primer or probe.
Building blocks of DNA, made from ribonucleotides by ribonucleotide reductase.
Labeled RNA strand used to detect complementary nucleic acid sequences.
Labeled probe binding to nucleic acid sequences in intact tissue.
Technique using fluorescent probes to detect specific chromosomal sequences, deletions or translocations.
Mouse with foreign DNA inserted into its genome to study gene function.
Pattern of histone modifications, such as acetylation and methylation, regulating gene expression.
RNA over 200 nucleotides that does not code for protein but regulates gene expression, such as XIST.
Mixture of normal and mutated mitochondrial DNA in a cell; disease severity depends on the proportion.
Muscle diseases from mitochondrial DNA defects, causing weakness and lactic acidosis, with ragged red fibers.
Blood types set by A and B sugar antigens on red cells; plasma has antibodies to the antigens absent.
Same phenotype caused by different genetic variants (allelic) or different genes (locus).
Gene in the Prader-Willi region of chromosome 15, expressed only from the paternal allele.
Psychiatric disorder of repetitive skin picking causing lesions.
Region where sister chromatids join and spindle fibers attach.
Deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5, with a high-pitched cat-like cry and intellectual disability.
Extracellular matrix glycoprotein forming microfibrils; mutated in Marfan syndrome.
Outward protrusion of the sternum (pigeon chest).
Fluid at the fetal neck on ultrasound; increased thickness suggests Down syndrome.
Speed of the pulse wave between carotid and femoral arteries; measures aortic stiffness.
Speed of the arterial pressure wave; higher values indicate stiffer arteries.
Gi-coupled acetylcholine receptor in the heart that slows heart rate.
Troponin subunit binding calcium, initiating muscle contraction.
Pumps calcium out of the cytosol; SERCA pumps it into the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Local anesthetic injected into the subarachnoid space, blocking sensation below the injection level.
Kidney segment reabsorbing most filtered sodium, water, glucose and bicarbonate.
Accessory pathway activating ventricles early, as in Wolff-Parkinson-White.
Rate red cells settle in plasma; raised in inflammation.
Branches of the ophthalmic artery supplying the eye's uvea.
Inflammation of blood vessel walls throughout the body.
Narrowing of coronary arteries, usually from atherosclerosis, causing angina.
Device implanted under the skin that shocks life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.
Sudden breathlessness waking a patient at night, a sign of left heart failure.
Sterile fibrin vegetations on valves in hypercoagulable states such as cancer.
Mechanical pump supporting a failing ventricle.
Thick filament protein; mutations cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Device delivering electric shock to restore a normal rhythm in ventricular fibrillation.
Wall separating left and right ventricles; defects cause VSD.
Fibrosis of the endocardium causing restrictive cardiomyopathy, common in tropical regions.
Thickening of the endocardium by collagen and elastin in infants, causing heart failure.
Abnormal skin reaction to sunlight, sometimes caused by drugs.
Drugs such as milrinone and cilostazol that raise cAMP, causing vasodilation and increased heart contractility.
Cyanotic heart defect with aorta from the right ventricle and pulmonary artery from the left ventricle; needs a shunt for survival.
Enzyme making histamine from histidine in mast cells.
Amino acids with positively charged side chains at physiological pH: arginine, lysine and histidine.
Docking proteins phosphorylated by the insulin receptor, relaying signals to PI3K.
Antigen-binding arm of an antibody containing variable regions.
Calcium channel blockers (amlodipine, nifedipine) acting mainly on vascular smooth muscle.
Long-acting thiazide-like diuretic used for hypertension.
Intermediate in cholesterol synthesis made by HMG-CoA reductase, the statin target.
Newly formed, disc-shaped HDL particle with little cholesterol, made in liver and gut.
Plasma protein moving cholesterol esters from HDL to VLDL and LDL.
Statin inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase to lower LDL.
Bile acid sequestrant lowering LDL; also lowers glucose.
Bile acid sequestrant for high LDL; can raise triglycerides.
Dephosphorylates myosin light chain, relaxing smooth muscle.
Regulatory myosin subunit; phosphorylation triggers smooth muscle contraction.
Lipid mixture (mainly dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine) from type II pneumocytes that lowers alveolar surface tension, preventing collapse.
Asthma, nasal polyps and aspirin sensitivity from shifts toward leukotrienes.
Rheumatoid arthritis with pneumoconiosis, producing lung nodules.
Eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions of damaged keratin in hepatocytes, seen in alcoholic hepatitis.
Painful, itchy skin lesions on fingers or toes after cold exposure.
Sarcoidosis presentation with fever, parotid enlargement and uveitis.
Converts angiotensin I to II and breaks down bradykinin; inhibited by ACE inhibitors.
Fluid recovered from washing the lung airways, analyzed for cells and organisms.
Ratio of helper to cytotoxic T cells; low in HIV, high in sarcoidosis lavage.
Carcinogens from combustion and smoke, such as benzo[a]pyrene.
Aromatic amine dye chemical that causes bladder cancer.
Increase in gene copy number, as with HER2 and N-myc in cancer.
Inflammation of the periosteum, the bone covering.
Unequal pupil sizes.
Calcium-binding protein used as an immunohistochemical marker for mesothelioma.
Keratin of basal epidermal cells; mutated in epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
Stabilizes fibrin clots by cross-linking; deficiency delays bleeding.
Intrinsic pathway factor; deficiency is hemophilia C.
Vitamin K-dependent clotting factor; deficiency is hemophilia B.
Platelet surface receptors such as GpIb and GpIIb/IIIa.
Enzyme regenerating active vitamin K; target of warfarin.
Antifibrinolytic that inhibits plasminogen activation.
Activated factor VIII, cofactor of factor IXa.
Enzyme that rearranges atoms within a molecule to form an isomer.
Vitamin B12 form; antidote for cyanide poisoning.
Heat-producing adipose tissue rich in mitochondria and UCP1.
UCP1, uncoupling oxidative phosphorylation to make heat in brown fat.
Enzyme forming alpha-1,6 branches in glycogen; deficiency causes Andersen disease.
Branching enzyme deficiency, causing abnormal glycogen, liver failure and cirrhosis in infancy.
Cytochrome P450 enzyme metabolizing ethanol and acetaminophen; induced by chronic alcohol use.
Vesicles of endoplasmic reticulum formed on homogenization, holding drug metabolizing enzymes.
Vesicles from liver ER containing cytochrome P450 enzymes.
Activated factor V, cofactor of factor Xa; resistant to protein C in factor V Leiden.
Test measuring fibrin clot formation after thrombin is added; prolonged by heparin.
Low molecular weight heparin that inhibits factor Xa.
Lower motor neurons in the spinal cord; destroyed in polio and ALS.
Constant air pressure through a mask that keeps the airway open, used for sleep apnea.
Oral appliance that moves the lower jaw forward to widen the airway in sleep apnea.
Sedating first-generation antihistamine for motion sickness.
First-generation H1 antihistamine, causing sedation and anticholinergic effects.
First-generation antihistamine and antiemetic.
Second-generation H1 antihistamine with little sedation.
Inhaled corticosteroid for asthma.
Combination inhaler of corticosteroid and long-acting beta agonist.
Combination inhaler of corticosteroid and long-acting beta agonist.
Anti-IgE monoclonal antibody for allergic asthma.
Expectorant that thins airway mucus.
Ion channel (AMPA, NMDA, kainate) and G-protein receptors for glutamate.
Intracellular receptors modulating neurotransmission, targeted by some psychoactive drugs.
ACE inhibitor for hypertension and heart failure; can cause cough and angioedema.
Plasma protein cleaved by kallikrein to make bradykinin.
Drugs such as aliskiren that block renin and lower angiotensin.
Enzyme degrading heparan sulfate, aiding tumor invasion.
Membrane proteins moving glucose, such as GLUT4 (insulin-responsive).
Loop diuretic inhibiting NKCC2.
Excess phosphate in urine, seen in X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets.
Partial nicotinic receptor agonist for smoking cessation.
Enzyme converting glutamine to glutamate and ammonia; important in the kidney.
Cell surface mucin, marker for breast and other adenocarcinomas.
Autoantibody stabilizing C3 convertase, causing low C3 and membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis.
Chronic kidney infection with lipid-laden macrophages, associated with stones and Proteus.
Diuretics such as mannitol that increase tubular osmolarity, pulling water into urine.
Anion exchanger swapping chloride for bicarbonate; in the kidney's alpha-intercalated cells and red cells.
Licorice compound inhibiting 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, causing pseudohyperaldosteronism.
Solvent that can cause anion gap acidosis with high doses of lorazepam infusion.
Tests of bladder pressure and flow to evaluate urinary function.
Receptors on macrophages taking up oxidized LDL, forming foam cells.
Two defective LDL receptor genes, with severe early cholesterol elevations and early heart disease.
Enzyme making HMG-CoA in ketone body synthesis and cholesterol synthesis.
Nutrient that is a precursor of acetylcholine and phosphatidylcholine.
Lipid that accumulates in Tay-Sachs (hexosaminidase A) and Sandhoff diseases.
Sphingomyelinase deficiency causing sphingomyelin accumulation, hepatosplenomegaly and neurodegeneration, with a cherry-red macula.
